## Glossary

**atlas**  
Class: Atlas code map: concept vocabulary, @atlas annotations, navigating by concept.

**@atlas block**  
Top-of-file JSDoc annotation declaring @kind, @partOf, @uses, @constructs; the only standing comment template allows.

**atlas check**  
Gate verifying blocks exist and use valid vocabulary, not correctness.

**atlas stamp**  
Fills @kind/@partOf from .atlas/config.ts rules; dry-run by default, --write applies, never touches @uses.

**build-tooling**  
Class: Turborepo tasks, watch mode, codegen, build presets, hot reload.

**bun run check**  
The full gate: lint, typecheck, test, test:fe and run-ci-rules.sh.

**check-import-aliases**  
Fails on relative internal imports that should use #/ or @template/.

**code-style**  
Class: formatting, no comments, TypeScript rules, imports.

**CONCEPTS**  
.atlas/concepts.ts registry, class:name → module/package/docs; structure only, broad but closed.

**config sync / config check**  
Apply versions.json pins and presets locally / verify them read-only.

**.gen. files**  
Template-owned generated files, ignored by git, lint, search and turbo task inputs.

**Generation chain**  
turbo dependsOn ordering db:generate → generate:openapi → generate:sdk, then app restarts.

**gloss**  
Class: writing glosses (@inixiative/gloss): margin commentary in .gloss/ sidecars.

**// gloss dagger**  
Content-free marker that a symbol (or, as // gloss:file, a file) has a gloss section.

**keyof typeof**  
Derive a union type from a const object so values live in one place.

**@kind**  
The file's role from .atlas/kinds.ts (controller, service, registry...), never a layer.

**lefthook**  
Pre-commit hooks from @inixiative/config/lefthook/base.yml running typecheck and Biome on staged files.

**lint-rules**  
Class: Biome, custom lint scripts and the CI rule runner that enforce style.

**MAP.md**  
Generated concept map at the repo root (atlas generate); never hand-edited.

**_name / __name**  
Single underscore = unused binding; double underscore = private/internal.

**naming**  
Class: naming conventions for identifiers, files, routes, schema names, polymorphic side names, vocabulary.

**@partOf**  
Concepts the file is a member of; removing the file breaks them.

**Polymorphic sides**  
owner (tenancy), source/target (edge ends), resource, subject, actor as `<side>Model` plus side-prefixed FKs and relations; never referenced*.

**resourceActionSubresource**  
Route/operationId pattern: userCreate, organizationReadManySpaces, adminOrganizationReadMany.

**rule-violations fixtures**  
scripts/ci/rule-violations/<rule>/pass and /fail cases; protected along with the rules.

**run-ci-rules.sh**  
Runs scripts/ci/rules alphabetically; --test checks each rule against its pass/fail fixtures.

**run-post-biome-checks**  
Runs check-import-aliases, check-generated-files and check-finder-duplicates after Biome.

**scripts**  
Class: the sanctioned package.json scripts and how to run and write them.

**@uses**  
Load-bearing concept dependencies, hand-curated; `@uses none` = looked and found none.

**// why:**  
The one inline gloss-convention comment: a load-bearing constraint the code cannot show.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The tools an agent uses while changing template code and the conventions those tools apply: the package.json scripts, Biome with the custom lint scripts and CI rules, the Turborepo task graph and the shared @inixiative/config presets, the Atlas code map and its annotations, gloss, and the naming and code-style rules.

## 2. The domain

`scripts` is the sanctioned command surface in the root package.json: run things from the root (`turbo watch` gives workspace-aware reload; running inside one app only watches that app), `start:api` / `start:worker` / `start:web` are production runs, and new shell scripts go in `scripts/<category>/` (made executable), TypeScript scripts run with `bun run <path>`, throwaway ones in gitignored `tmp/`. `lint-rules` is the enforcement: `bun run lint` is Biome on the `@inixiative/config` biome presets plus `run-post-biome-checks` (`check-import-aliases`, `check-generated-files`, `check-finder-duplicates`); `lint:fix` applies fixes, `format` only formats; `bun run check` is the full gate (lint, typecheck, test, test:fe, then `scripts/ci/run-ci-rules.sh`). CI rules in `scripts/ci/rules` run alphabetically and each has pass/fail fixtures in `scripts/ci/rule-violations/<rule>/`, checked by `run-ci-rules.sh --test`; those paths are protected, so a failing rule is fixed in the source, never by editing the rule or its fixtures. Lefthook runs typecheck and Biome on staged files through `@inixiative/config/lefthook/base.yml`. Template commits no CI workflow yet (CICD.md; `.github/` holds only FUNDING.yml), so `bun run check` run locally is the gate; `lib-ci.yml` is the config repo's caller for library repos. `build-tooling` is Turborepo plus the shared presets: turbo task names match package scripts, `#pkg` filters to one package, `dependsOn` chains `db:generate` → `generate:openapi` → `generate:sdk` so schema changes cascade, generated files carry `.gen.` and are excluded from task inputs to prevent loops, generation and build tasks are cached; workspace tsconfigs extend `@inixiative/config/tsconfig/base.json` or `react.json` and hold only extends, paths and include; tsup configs call the `node` or `react` preset; toolchain versions are pinned at the root by `versions.json`, applied with `config sync` and verified with `config check`.

`atlas` is how you find what already exists by concept and keep the map true: every file has a top-of-file `@atlas` block (`@kind` = role from `.atlas/kinds.ts`, never a layer; `@partOf` = the concepts that break without the file; `@uses` = load-bearing dependencies only, curated by hand, `@uses none` only after looking; `@constructs` for factories). Concepts are `class:name` (`feature:`, `primitive:`, `infrastructure:`, `integration:`, plus `superadmin`) in the closed, structure-only registry `.atlas/concepts.ts`; `atlas stamp` fills `@kind`/`@partOf` from `.atlas/config.ts` rules (dry-run by default, never touches `@uses`); `MAP.md` is generated; navigate with `bunx atlas graph --json` and `bunx atlas query` before grepping; `atlas check` gates existence and vocabulary, not correctness. `gloss` is the @inixiative/gloss convention: commentary lives in a `.gloss/<path>.md` sidecar, source keeps only `// why:` lines, `// gloss` daggers and machine directives, `gloss read` reads it and `gloss fix` repairs it (never delete a section or dagger to green a check). Template does not depend on gloss and has no `.gloss/`, so in template the stricter AI/ENTRYPOINT.md rule applies: no comments except the `@atlas` block and a rare one-line non-obvious why. `naming` is the vocabulary: operationIds and route files as `resourceActionSubresource` (singular resource, plural ReadMany subresource), hooks `<model><Timing><Purpose>`, jobs `<verb><Noun>`, `util` not helper, `services` not handlers, `make*` factories, `validate*` guards, `get*`/`is*`, `txn`, `<Model>Id`, SCREAMING_SNAKE primitives and PascalCase const objects with `keyof typeof` types, PascalCase singular Prisma models with camelCase fields and no `@map` (`no-prisma-maps`), polymorphic sides `owner` (tenancy only) / `source`/`target` / `resource` / `subject` / `actor` carried into FKs and back-relations, never `referenced*`; `_name` = unused, `__name` = internal. `code-style` is semicolons, single quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, typed arrow functions, named exports, one file per concern, single-line early exits, `type` over `interface`, no TS `enum`, types inferred from Zod/Prisma, no `any`, index files only at module/package level, quiet one-line logging.

Related regions: `lib-atlas`, `lib-gloss` and `lib-config` hold those libraries' full READMEs (CLI flags, config API, the release `train`, lanes); `monorepo-architecture` holds where code lives, the workspace map and the import-alias and tsconfig-paths rules these lint scripts enforce; `dx-setup` holds setup, running locally, env and worktrees; `engineering-process-docs` holds the working method (reuse what exists, verification) and the docs workflow; a CI rule that guards a domain (create races, env coercion, test mocks) is explained by that domain's region (`concurrency-locks`, `dx-setup`, `testing`).

## 3. Everything that exists here, by class

Point at a class when that is as specific as the moment allows, or at a member. Each member: **name** `where`: choose this when … . Where the docs or code give material, a second line describes the hand-rolled code an agent writes when it rebuilds the primitive instead of using it. Code members come from the catalog, described from the code. Doc members are named in the doc sections in part 4. *Also here, by name* lists the parts of a larger system.

### Class `scripts`: The sanctioned package.json scripts and how to run and write them

- **bun run reset:db** `package.json`: Full fresh local DB; start:db just boots containers, db:push alone keeps existing data.
- **bun run start:api** `package.json`: API HTTP process only; start:worker for background jobs, start:web for the frontend preview.
- **bun run start:db** `package.json`: Identical to local:db; reset:db when you also need schema push and seed.
- **bun run start:web** `package.json`: Previews the production build; run build first.
- **bun run start:worker** `package.json`: Job processing only; start:api serves HTTP requests.
- **bun run stop:db** `package.json`: Teardown only; reset:db to recreate with schema and seed.

### Class `lint-rules`: Biome, custom lint scripts and the CI rule runner that enforce style

- **check-finder-duplicates** `scripts/lint/check-finder-duplicates.sh`: Stale or uncommitted generated output: check-generated-files instead.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* committed 'routeTree.gen 2.ts' or 'dist 2' copies, or deleting such duplicates by hand one at a time (catalog check-finder-duplicates)
- **check-generated-files** `scripts/lint/check-generated-files.sh`: Sync-conflict copies like 'x.gen 2.ts': check-finder-duplicates instead.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* committing a schema or route change without regenerating, or hand-editing the Prisma client or OpenAPI SDK (scripts/lint/check-generated-files.sh; FEATURES.md › Custom Lint Checks)
- **check-import-aliases** `scripts/lint/check-import-aliases.sh`: require path aliases instead of relative imports
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `import { x } from '../../lib/utils/x'` or `'../shared/src/...'` in a non-barrel source file (scripts/lint/check-import-aliases.sh; docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md § Linting)
- **no-isarray-cast** `scripts/ci/rules/no-isarray-cast.sh`: CI check forbidding casts after Array.isArray narrowing
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `Array.isArray(value) ? (value as Foo[])` or `as unknown[]` right after an isArray check (scripts/ci/rules/no-isarray-cast.sh (CI rule))
- **run-post-biome-checks** `scripts/lint/run-post-biome-checks.sh`: Runs all script checks together; call an individual check-*.sh only to debug one rule.
- **bun run build** `package.json`: build every workspace app and package for production
- **bun run check** `package.json`: Before pushing: check instead of running lint, typecheck or tests individually.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* running lint, typecheck or a subset of tests individually and calling the change green (catalog `bun run check`; root CLAUDE.md merging rules (full check))
- **bun run deploy** `package.json`: deploy the project via the deployment script
- **bun run format** `package.json`: Formatting only; lint:fix to also apply lint fixes.
- **bun run lint** `package.json`: Report only; lint:fix to auto-apply fixes; check for the full gate.
- **bun run lint:fix** `package.json`: Fixes lint and formatting; format only reformats; lint only reports.
- **bun run lint:generated** `package.json`: Targeted generated-file check; lint for everything.
- **bun run lint:imports** `package.json`: Targeted import-alias check; lint for everything.
- **bun run typecheck** `package.json`: Whole-repo check; frontend apps only after route regen: typecheck:fe. Same as tsc alias.
- **bun run typecheck:fe** `package.json`: Frontend apps only, with fresh generated routes; whole repo: typecheck instead.
- **Consumer sync via review branch** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: land consumer ecosystem bumps through a reviewed branch, never publishing
- **Release lanes in dependency order, config last** `@inixiative/config/README.md#Release flow`: use --lane=agentic to leave primitives untouched
- **Workspace member publish** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: publish workspace packages with workspace: ranges rewritten to released versions
- **@inixiative/config/biome/base.json** `@inixiative/config/biome/base.json`: every repo; add biome/react.json overlay for React code.
- **@inixiative/config/biome/react.json** `@inixiative/config/biome/react.json`: React packages only; base.json alone elsewhere.
- **@inixiative/config/lefthook/base.yml** `@inixiative/config/lefthook/base.yml`: run typecheck and biome on staged files at pre-commit
- **bun run start** `apps/api package.json scripts`: production; local dev: bun run local
- **bun run start:<service>** `package.json`: Production runs; development uses bun run local or turbo watch.
- **check-generated-files.sh** `scripts/lint/check-generated-files.sh`: fail when Prisma client or OpenAPI SDK are out of date
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* committing a schema or route change without regenerating, or hand-editing the Prisma client or OpenAPI SDK (scripts/lint/check-generated-files.sh; FEATURES.md › Custom Lint Checks)
- **check-import-aliases.sh** `scripts/lint/check-import-aliases.sh`: fail on relative internal imports not using the #/ alias
- **config scan** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: multi-repo audit; check for a single repo, train to actually release
- **config train** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: releasing ecosystem packages; scan only reports drift without publishing
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* running `npm publish` or `bun publish` by hand for an @inixiative/* package, or bumping dependents one by one, instead of bumping the version and running train (@inixiative/config/README.md § Release flow ("A release is train"))
- **inixiative-config check** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CI`: verify a repo's toolchain coherence and lockfile format
- **inixiative-config train** `@inixiative/config/README.md#Release flow`: releasing packages; downstream toolchain pickup without release: sync instead.
- **lib-ci.yml** `inixiative/config/.github/workflows/lib-ci.yml`: run pinned bun, frozen install, config check and repo check in CI
- **Root workspace scripts** `FEATURES.md > Core Platform > Workspace Tooling`: lint, typecheck or test every package from the repo root
- **run-ci-rules.sh** `scripts/ci/run-ci-rules.sh`: --test to verify rules against pass/fail fixtures
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a new rule script under scripts/ci/rules with no pass/fail cases in scripts/ci/rule-violations, or a fixture edited so a failing rule passes (docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md § CI Rule Scripts; AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 0.0 Critical Guardrails)
- **run-post-biome-checks.sh** `scripts/lint/run-post-biome-checks.sh`: run all; individual scripts for one check
- **scripts/deployment/deploy.sh** `scripts/deployment/deploy.sh`: deploy to a target environment
- **scripts/deployment/wait-for-api.sh** `scripts/deployment/wait-for-api.sh`: wait until the API health check passes
- **train --dry-run** `@inixiative/config/README.md`: print each planned release step without running any
- **train --push** `@inixiative/config/README.md`: omit to only print the push commands.
- **atlas check in CI** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#CLI`: Every CI run and before pushing annotation changes.
- **Commands reject foreign flags** `@inixiative/config/README.md`: every inixiative-config command
- **Commit up-to-date generated files** `scripts/lint/check-generated-files.sh`: after schema or route changes
- **Fix the cause directly** `CLAUDE.md § 0.0 Critical Guardrails`: Any breakage or failure encountered during work.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `git stash` to compare against HEAD, reverting changes to bisect, or editing scripts/ci/rules or rule-violations fixtures to make a failure pass (AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 0.0 Critical Guardrails)
- **Frozen lockfile installs in CI** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CI`: all lib repo CI
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a CI job running plain `bun install` (lockfile can drift) before checks (@inixiative/config/README.md § CI)
- **Import aliases** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Backend > Imports`: Every import; relative paths only in top-level barrel index.ts re-exports.
- **Imports follow alias rules** `CLAUDE.md §13 Change Checklist`: Any added or moved import.
- **Lanes cascade one way** `@inixiative/config/README.md#versions.json (the BOM)`: publishing or depending across @inixiative lanes
- **Launch preflight gate** `docs/claude/INIT_SCRIPT_PATTERNS.md > Current implementation notes`: Launching a provisioned project.
- **Lib repos use the shared CI caller** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CI`: every lib repo
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a lib repo with its own full CI workflow installing bun, deps and running checks, instead of the two-line caller of inixiative/config/.github/workflows/lib-ci.yml (@inixiative/config/README.md § CI)
- **No any; canonical types** `CLAUDE.md §7 Core Engineering Standards`: Avoid any and import canonical types from source modules.
- **No code comments** `CLAUDE.md § 0. Purpose and Priority`: All source files; @atlas annotation block is the sole standing exception.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* comments narrating what the next line does, restating a function name, or section-divider and reasoning comments (AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 0. Purpose and Priority; docs/claude/STYLE.md § Comments & Logging)
- **No git commands unless asked** `CLAUDE.md § 0.0 Critical Guardrails`: Any comparison against HEAD or clean state.
- **No intermediate barrels** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Backend > Imports`: Any import that could go through a non-top-level index file.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a new nested index.ts re-exporting siblings, or imports from '#/lib' instead of the source file (docs/claude/NAMING.md › Backend › Imports; docs/claude/STYLE.md › Minimal Index Files)
- **No scope invention** `CLAUDE.md §0.3 YAGNI — Scope Invention vs. Completion`: Feature code leans trim; clearly adjacent noise is skipped.
- **Path aliases** `docs/claude/MONOREPO.md#path-aliases`: Import with #/ inside apps, @template/<pkg>/* elsewhere, relative only in barrels.
- **Run check in CI** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: CI pipelines of ecosystem repos.
- **Train ships default branch from origin** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: Releasing via train.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* publishing a package from a feature branch or a checkout behind origin (@inixiative/config/README.md § CLI (train only ships the default branch))
- **TypeScript strict, no any** `FEATURES.md > Core Platform > TypeScript Strict Mode`: All application code in every package.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `: any`, `as any`, or `as unknown as T` to silence the compiler (FEATURES.md › TypeScript Strict Mode; AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 7)
- **Use #/ alias, not relative imports** `scripts/lint/check-import-aliases.sh`: all internal TypeScript imports
- *Also here, by name:* bun run lint:postBiome (`package.json`); bun run tsc (`package.json`)

### Class `build-tooling`: Turborepo tasks, watch mode, codegen, build presets, hot reload

- **node** `@inixiative/config/tsup#node`: Node/server packages; React UI packages: react preset instead. Extend rather than writing per-package tsup config.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a per-package tsup.config.ts spelling out format, dts, target and externals instead of `export default node({ entry })` (@inixiative/config/tsup#node (catalog); @inixiative/config/README.md#Presets)
- **react** `@inixiative/config/tsup#react`: React/UI packages; non-UI packages: node preset instead.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-written tsup config for a React/UI package instead of `export default react({ entry })` (@inixiative/config/tsup#react (catalog))
- **Adopt config via extends stubs** `@inixiative/config/README.md#Presets`: adopt shared toolchain with tsconfig, biome, tsup stub files plus devDependency
- **Env composition with turbo watch** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#Environment Composition with Turbo`: Pointing local apps at prod/staging/test env; plain turbo watch for local env.
- **Generation chain via dependsOn** `turbo.json`: cascade schema changes through db:generate, generate:openapi, generate:sdk, then restart apps
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a script that runs db:generate, generate:openapi and generate:sdk in sequence by hand, or a new generator step wired outside turbo.json dependsOn (docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md § Task Dependencies; § Watch Mode › How it works)
- **@inixiative/config/tsconfig/base.json** `@inixiative/config/tsconfig/base.json`: bun libraries; node.json for node types, react.json for DOM/JSX packages.
- **@inixiative/config/tsconfig/node.json** `@inixiative/config/tsconfig/node.json`: packages needing node types; base.json for pure bun, react.json for DOM/JSX.
- **@inixiative/config/tsconfig/react.json** `@inixiative/config/tsconfig/react.json`: React/DOM packages; base.json or node.json otherwise.
- **build / typecheck / test** `turbo.json`: run cached production build, type checking and test suites across apps
- **bun run local** `package.json`: Full-stack local dev; turbo watch local#<pkg> for one app.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `cd apps/api && bun --hot src/index.ts` as the dev loop, which does not watch workspace package changes (docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md § Development (Direct execution note))
- **config check** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: read-only CI gate; use sync to apply fixes, scan for all checkouts
- **config sync** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: to fix drift locally; check only reports; refuses dirty tree without --force
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-editing package.json versions or preset files to match versions.json (@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI)
- **db:generate** `turbo.json`: generate Prisma client and Zod schemas from schema.prisma, cached
- **generate:openapi** `turbo.json`: produce the OpenAPI spec from API routes
- **generate:routes** `turbo.json`: produce the TanStack Router route tree
- **generate:sdk** `turbo.json`: produce the TypeScript API client from the OpenAPI spec
- **inixiative-config sync** `@inixiative/config/README.md#Release flow`: downstream adoption of toolchain changes; publishing releases: train instead.
- **start:api / start:worker / start:web** `package.json`: Production runs; local dev uses bun run local instead.
- **sync** `@inixiative/config/README.md#@inixiative/config`: to update pins; check to verify without writing.
- **turbo run --graph / --output-logs / --force** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#Debugging`: inspect the task graph, show full logs, or bypass the cache
- **turbo watch local#pkg** `turbo.json`: Single app dev; bun run local for the full stack; local:worker#api for the worker.
- **versions.json** `@inixiative/config/versions.json`: pin bun, toolchain, required packages, lane sets and consumer repos
- **@types/bun required with TS 6** `@inixiative/config/README.md#versions.json (the BOM)`: all repos on TypeScript 6.0
- **CLI vs Renovate division** `@inixiative/config/README.md`: dependency updates in any lib repo
- **Ecosystem deps at blessed versions** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: Root and workspace members of either lane; workspace:/file:/link: exempt.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an @inixiative/* dependency bumped to a version other than the one versions.json blesses (@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI)
- **Generated files use .gen. and are excluded from inputs** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#Loop Prevention`: Any template-owned generated file; Prisma-owned internals exempt unless generator emits .gen.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a new generated file without `.gen.` in its name, or a turbo inputs glob that includes generated output so watch mode regenerates forever (docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md § Loop Prevention)
- **Repos held to union of lanes** `@inixiative/config/README.md#versions.json (the BOM)`: repos mixing primitives and agentic packages
- **Required repo scaffolding** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: Every ecosystem repo.
- **Scope ignoreDeprecations to dts build** `@inixiative/config/tsup`: tsup builds under TypeScript 6.0
- **Stubs hold only extends and reviewed overrides** `@inixiative/config/README.md#Presets`: every repo adopting @inixiative/config
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a repo's biome.json or tsconfig copied wholesale from the preset with drifted local edits (@inixiative/config/README.md#Presets)
- **Toolchain pins at root only** `@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI`: Any repo in the ecosystem declaring toolchain dependencies.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* typescript, @biomejs/biome or @types/bun declared in a workspace package.json (@inixiative/config/README.md#CLI)
- **Turbo task names match package scripts** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#Task Naming Convention`: When adding a script or turbo task to any package.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a turbo.json task named differently from the package.json script it should run, or a script using a delimiter other than `:` (docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md § Task Naming Convention)

### Class `atlas`: Atlas code map: concept vocabulary, @atlas annotations, navigating by concept

- **defineConfig** `@inixiative/atlas#defineConfig`: Same function as @inixiative/atlas/config#defineConfig; prefer the root import.
- **parseAtlasBlock** `@inixiative/atlas#parseAtlasBlock`: parse an Atlas annotation block from source or docs
- **partOfFor** `@inixiative/atlas#partOfFor`: Use instead of listing explicit concepts per rule; re-export of @inixiative/atlas/config#partOfFor.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* stamp rules listing explicit concepts per path instead of capturing module/package with partOfFor('module', '$1') (catalog @inixiative/atlas#partOfFor; docs/claude/ATLAS.md § The .atlas/ config)
- **@atlas annotation block** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#Writing a block`: declare a file's role, membership and load-bearing dependencies for the code map
- **Atlas CI rollout** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#CI`: adopt atlas enforcement gradually on existing codebases
- **Navigate by concept before grep** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#For AI agents`: For 'what touches X' / 'what's part of Y' questions, including transitive edges; grep only as fallback.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* repeated rg/grep sweeps to answer 'what is part of Y' instead of `bunx atlas query --partOf ...` or conceptToFiles from `atlas graph --json` (@inixiative/atlas/README.md#For AI agents; docs/claude/ATLAS.md § Navigating by concept)
- **.atlas/config.ts** `.atlas/config.ts`: derivable tags per path; concepts.ts for concept definitions, kinds.ts for vocabulary
- **.atlas/kinds.ts** `.atlas/kinds.ts`: define the repo's @kind vocabulary extending atlas defaults
- **@atlas pin** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#The patcher: atlas stamp`: exempt a block from atlas stamp --overwrite resyncing
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an exception block that atlas stamp --overwrite keeps rewriting, handled by re-editing it after every stamp instead of adding @atlas pin (@inixiative/atlas/README.md § The patcher: atlas stamp)
- **atlas check** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#CI`: Checks existence/vocab only, not correctness; use atlas coverage for annotation percentage gates.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a custom CI script that greps files for @atlas blocks or validates tags against a list, instead of running atlas check (@inixiative/atlas/README.md § CI; examples/ci/README.md ("atlas check is the CI primitive"))
- **atlas coverage** `@inixiative/atlas CLI`: Gap lists or ratchet gates; atlas report for visual COVERAGE.md and atlas.html.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-counted annotation percentage or a script listing unannotated files, instead of atlas coverage --min / --ratchet (@inixiative/atlas/examples/ci/README.md § Coverage gate)
- **atlas generate** `@inixiative/atlas CLI`: write MAP.md concept overview from the annotated tree
- **atlas graph** `@inixiative/atlas CLI`: Querying relations; atlas generate for the readable overview.
- **atlas query** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — bunx atlas query`: Filtering files by axis combos; whole-concept reverse indexes: atlas graph instead. Prefer over grep.
- **atlas report** `@inixiative/atlas CLI`: Visual per-concept work plans; atlas coverage for plain gap listings.
- **atlas stamp** `@inixiative/atlas CLI`: Bulk annotating from path rules; add --overwrite only to replace existing blocks; hand-write for exceptions.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-writing @kind/@partOf on many files that the .atlas/config.ts rules would derive (docs/claude/ATLAS.md § Authoring annotations)
- **atlas stamp --overwrite** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — bunx atlas stamp`: after rules change; default additive stamp only fills absent tags
- **bunx atlas graph** `CLAUDE.md §11.5 Atlas — the code map`: Whole-map analysis; bunx atlas query for a single concept.
- **bunx atlas query** `CLAUDE.md §11.5 Atlas — the code map`: Targeted concept lookup; bunx atlas graph --json for the whole graph, MAP.md for browsing.
- **Concept registry** `.atlas/concepts.ts`: Structure only, no status; keep vocabulary broad but closed rather than adding hyper-specific labels.
- **ConceptRegistry** `.atlas/concepts.ts`: type the repo-owned map of concepts to constituent modules and docs
- **CONCEPTS** `.atlas/concepts.ts`: registry of concepts keyed class:name with module, package or docs
- **KINDS** `.atlas/kinds.ts`: declare allowed @kind vocabulary extending atlas defaults
- **kinds.ts** `.atlas/kinds.ts`: define the closed enum of allowed @kind role values, extending DEFAULT_KINDS
- **MAP.md** `MAP.md (repo root)`: High-altitude overview before opening the tree; precise lookups: atlas graph or query.
- **@atlas file annotation block** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#atlas`: All files matched by .atlas/config.ts include globs, excluding ignored tests and index files.
- **@constructs for factories only** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — @constructs — factory output`: Factory/constructor files only.
- **@kind is a role, never a layer** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#Writing a block`: Every @atlas block's @kind line.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `@kind feature` / `@kind primitive` / `@kind infrastructure` in an @atlas block (docs/claude/ATLAS.md § @kind — the role)
- **@partOf is membership** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#Writing a block`: Concepts that break if the file is removed; use @uses for mere dependencies.
- **@partOf membership** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — @partOf — membership`: Concepts that break without this file; dependencies go in @uses instead.
- **@uses is load-bearing only** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#Writing a block`: Skip incidental touches like one db update via request context.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an @uses line listing every imported concept, including incidental db or logger touches (@inixiative/atlas/README.md#Writing a block; docs/claude/ATLAS.md § @uses)
- **@uses load-bearing only** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — @uses — load-bearing dependencies`: Dependencies the file relies on but isn't part of; skip incidental imports like one db update.
- **@uses none only after checking** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — Authoring rules`: When a file seems to use no concepts
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `@uses none` written on files nobody inspected, instead of omitting the line (uncurated) (docs/claude/ATLAS.md § Authoring rules)
- **Broad closed concept vocabulary** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#Why`: When choosing @partOf/@uses tags or proposing a new concept.
- **Concept registry is structure only** `.atlas/concepts.ts`: When adding or editing entries in .atlas/concepts.ts.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* status, maturity or TODO fields added to .atlas/concepts.ts, or a hyper-specific concept added for one file (docs/claude/ATLAS.md § The concept vocabulary; § What Atlas is)
- **Curate @uses by hand** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — bunx atlas stamp`: Whenever recording what a file uses
- **Explicit annotations win over stamp rules** `.atlas/config.ts`: When a stamped tag is wrong for a specific file.
- **Keep @atlas block true** `CLAUDE.md §11.5 Atlas — the code map`: Adding, moving or repurposing any file.
- **Keep @atlas block true on add/move** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — Authoring rules`: Any file added or moved
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a new or moved file with no @atlas block, or a stale @partOf left after moving a file to another module (docs/claude/ATLAS.md § Authoring rules; AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 11.5)
- **MAP.md is generated, not hand-edited** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#CLI`: Whenever annotations change; prefer this over hand-written FEATURES.md or prose maps.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* manual edits to MAP.md or a hand-written prose map of modules (@inixiative/atlas/README.md#CLI; docs/claude/ATLAS.md § Navigating by concept)
- **Navigate by Atlas concept before grepping** `CLAUDE.md §11.5 Atlas — the code map`: Locating existing code for any task.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* repeated rg/grep sweeps to answer 'what touches X' instead of `bunx atlas graph --json` / `bunx atlas query --uses ...` (AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 11.5; docs/claude/ATLAS.md § Navigating by concept)
- **Navigate by concept, not grep** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — Navigating by concept`: Concept-membership or dependency questions about the codebase.
- **Prefer broad-true tags** `@inixiative/atlas/README.md#Writing a block`: When choosing @partOf/@uses values.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* minting a new hyper-specific concept for one file instead of combining existing broad concepts (@inixiative/atlas/README.md § Why; § Writing a block)
- **Register unresolved concepts** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — bunx atlas stamp`: When a stamp capture resolves to no concept
- **Valid atlas vocabulary** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md — Authoring rules`: Writing any @atlas tag
- **Validate atlas names against .atlas/** `.atlas/kinds.ts, .atlas/concepts.ts`: Whenever writing or editing an @atlas block.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an @partOf or @uses naming a concept missing from .atlas/concepts.ts, or an @kind outside kinds.ts (docs/claude/ATLAS.md § Authoring rules; § Enforcement)
- *Also here, by name:* DEFAULT_KINDS (`@inixiative/atlas`); conceptClass (`@inixiative/atlas`); conceptClasses (`@inixiative/atlas`); defineConfig (`@inixiative/atlas/config`); invert (`@inixiative/atlas`); isPartOfFor (`@inixiative/atlas/config`); isPartOfFor (`@inixiative/atlas`); partOfFor (`@inixiative/atlas/config`)

### Class `naming`: Naming conventions: identifiers, files, routes, schema names, polymorphic side names, vocabulary

- **no-prisma-maps** `scripts/ci/rules/no-prisma-maps.sh`: Enum-value @map remains allowed for legacy stored strings.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `@map("snake_case_name")` on a field or `@@map("users")` on a model (scripts/ci/rules/no-prisma-maps.sh (CI rule))
- **Backend directory layout** `docs/claude/NAMING.md#Backend Structure`: Model-specific routes, hooks and jobs go in modules/<model>; cross-cutting jobs in src/jobs; route mounting in src/routes.
- **keyof typeof const objects** `apps/api/src/modules/batch/constants.ts`: Instead of hand-written string unions duplicating an object's keys.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-written string union that duplicates a const object's keys (docs/claude/NAMING.md › Backend › Constants Pattern: keyof typeof)
- **Backend file naming** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Backend > Files`: Any new backend file.
- **Backend function naming** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Backend > Functions`: Any new backend function.
- **Frontend component naming** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Frontend > Components`: Any new frontend component, hook or context file.
- **Never referenced* names** `docs/claude/NAMING.md#Polymorphic Sides`: Any polymorphic slot, FK or relation naming.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `referencedModel` / `referencedId` slot names instead of source/target, resource, subject or actor (docs/claude/NAMING.md § Polymorphic Sides)
- **No barrel files in lib** `docs/claude/NAMING.md#Backend Structure`: Any shared utility module under lib.
- **Plural ReadMany subresources** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Backend > Files`: Route handlers reading a list of a subresource.
- **Polymorphic side naming** `docs/claude/NAMING.md#Polymorphic Sides`: owner for tenancy only; source/target for directed edges; resource for one-sided slots; subject for what a record is about; actor for who acted.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `ownerModel` used for something other than tenancy, or a `type` + `id` string pair for a polymorphic slot (docs/claude/NAMING.md § Polymorphic Sides)
- **Preferred terminology** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Terminology`: All identifiers, folders and files; handlers only for jobs and frontend event handlers.
- **Prisma schema naming case** `docs/claude/NAMING.md#Prisma Schema`: Every Prisma model, enum, field and relation declaration.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* plural or snake_case model names, or snake_case fields in a .prisma file (docs/claude/NAMING.md § Database › Prisma Schema)
- **Rename misleading names** `CLAUDE.md § 0. Purpose and Priority`: Any identifier, file or API name that does not describe its behavior.
- **Side-prefixed FKs and back-relations** `docs/claude/NAMING.md#Polymorphic Sides`: Every typed FK and back-relation of a polymorphic model; models on both ends get both back-relations.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an edge model with unprefixed FKs like `segmentId` on both ends, or back-relations named `ruleReferences` instead of `sourceRuleReferences` / `targetRuleReferences` (docs/claude/NAMING.md § Polymorphic Sides)
- **Underscore prefix meanings** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Backend > Underscore Prefix`: Unused params/destructures: `_`; class privates, type brands, internal object keys: `__`; `#` only for runtime privacy.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `_cache` for module-private state, `__unused` for an ignored parameter, or `#private` fields without a need for runtime privacy (docs/claude/NAMING.md › Backend › Underscore Prefix)
- **Variable and constant casing** `docs/claude/NAMING.md > Backend > Variables`: Declaring types, constants, registries or derived helpers.

### Class `code-style`: Code style: formatting, no comments, TypeScript rules, imports

- **Single-line early exits** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Single-Line Early Exits`: Guard and bail out on one line before main logic.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* multi-line braced guard blocks or nested if/else before the main logic (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Single-Line Early Exits)
- **Atomic files** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Atomic Files`: Each file holds exactly one named export; helpers stay internal.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a utils.ts or helpers.ts exporting several unrelated functions for different consumers (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Atomic Files; AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 0 (One file, one concern))
- **Code formatting baseline** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Code Formatting`: Use semicolons, single quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, typed arrow functions.
- **Function and folder naming prefixes** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Naming Conventions`: Name util not helper, services not handlers, txn not transaction; make*/validate*/get*/is* prefixes.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a `helpers/` folder or `xHelper` name, a backend middleware guard named `require*`, or a transaction client named `tx` / `transaction` (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Naming Conventions; docs/claude/NAMING.md § Terminology)
- **Infer types from Zod and Prisma** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Infer Types`: Derive types from Zod schemas or Prisma instead of hand-writing them.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-written TypeScript interfaces/types that restate a zod schema or Prisma model (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Infer Types)
- **Minimal index files** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Minimal Index Files`: Index files exist only at module and package level, never nested.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an index.ts below module level (e.g. `#/hooks/webhooks/constants/index.ts`) re-exporting its folder (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Code Formatting › Minimal Index Files)
- **Minimal logging** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Minimal Logging`: Log one line per action, no ASCII art or emojis; scripts quiet.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* emoji or ASCII-art banners and step-by-step progress logs in scripts instead of errors or one final result (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Minimal Logging)
- **Named exports only** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Code Formatting`: Export symbols by name, never as default exports.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `export default function ...` or default-exported objects (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Code Formatting)
- **No comments** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#No Comments`: Omit code comments unless requested or truly non-obvious.
- **No root-level dependencies** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Dependencies`: Never install packages at repo root; add to the owning app or package.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `bun add <pkg>` at the repo root for a runtime dependency that one app or package imports (docs/claude/STYLE.md § Dependencies)
- **No TypeScript enum** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#No TypeScript enum`: Domain values: Prisma enum; local constant sets: as const object.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `enum Foo { ... }` in TypeScript for domain values instead of a Prisma enum or an `as const` object (docs/claude/STYLE.md § No TypeScript enum)
- **Path aliases, no relative imports** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Imports`: Same app/package: #/; other package: @template/* public entry.
- **type over interface** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#TypeScript`: Declare object shapes with type aliases, not interface.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `interface Foo { ... }` declarations for object shapes (docs/claude/STYLE.md § TypeScript)
- **Underscore variable prefixes** `docs/claude/STYLE.md#Variable Prefixes`: Prefix unused params with _ and unexported module-private state with __.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md#script-locations -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md` § Script Locations (in "Scripts & Commands")

#### Script Locations

| Directory | Purpose | Committed |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `scripts/` | Shared shell scripts, deployment, db ops | Yes |
| `init/` | Interactive infrastructure provisioning TUI (Bun + Ink) | Yes |
| `scripts/setup/` | Project initialization, env sync | Yes |
| `scripts/db/` | Postgres/Redis operations | Yes |
| `scripts/deployment/` | Deploy, env injection | Yes |
| `tmp/` | Temporary files, AI workspace, local experiments | No (.gitignore) |

##### scripts/ Structure

```
scripts/
├── setup/
│   ├── check-prereqs.sh    # Verify bun, docker, etc.
│   ├── setup.sh            # Full project setup
│   ├── sync-env.sh         # Sync .env from examples
│   └── init.sh             # Legacy shell bootstrap notes
├── db/
│   ├── dump.sh             # Export database
│   ├── restore.sh          # Import database
│   ├── clone.sh            # Clone remote → local (with webhook cleanup)
│   ├── push-dev.sh         # db:push:dev — worktree-aware, refuses non-local DATABASE_URLs
│   ├── release.sh          # Release-time database step
│   ├── pg-init.sh          # Postgres initialization
│   ├── minio-init.sh       # MinIO container entrypoint (creates the four base buckets)
│   ├── minio-provision.sh  # Ensure buckets exist (setup + worktree:create)
│   ├── minio-remove.sh     # Remove buckets, reporting each (worktree:destroy)
│   ├── wait-postgres.sh    # Wait for postgres ready
│   └── wait-redis.sh       # Wait for redis ready
├── deployment/
│   ├── deploy.sh           # Deploy to environment
│   ├── with-env.sh         # Run command with env vars
│   └── wait-for-api.sh     # Health check wait
└── worktree/
    ├── create.sh           # Provision an isolated worktree on a slot (DBs, buckets, env, deps, artifacts)
    ├── destroy.sh          # Tear a worktree down and free its slot
    ├── list.sh             # Worktrees with slot, branch, ports
    └── lib.sh              # Shared helpers (sourced by the three above)

init/
├── index.tsx                    # bun run init entrypoint
├── app.tsx                      # Ink app shell
├── tasks/                       # Provider setup logic
├── views/                       # Task/launch views
└── tests/                       # Fixtures and mocks

Database utilities (packages/db/prisma/):
├── seed.ts                       # Seed script with UUID validation
└── truncateWebhookSubscriptions.ts  # Clear webhooks (local/test only)
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md#development -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md` § Development (in "Scripts & Commands")

#### Development

From root `package.json`:

```bash
# Run all local services (api, web, worker, db)
bun run local

# Run specific services with Turborepo filtering
turbo watch local#api
turbo watch local#web
turbo watch local#admin
turbo watch local#superadmin
turbo watch local:worker#api

# Start database containers
bun run local:db        # docker-compose up -d --wait
```

**Development (from root):**
```bash
bun run local                              # All services with Turborepo watching
turbo watch local#api                      # Just API with hot reload
turbo watch local:worker#api               # Just worker with hot reload
bun run with prod api turbo watch local#api # API with prod env
```

**Production (from root):**
```bash
bun run start:api                          # Start API server
bun run start:worker                       # Start background worker
bun run start:web                          # Start web preview
```

**Direct execution (from apps/api):**
```bash
cd apps/api
bun run local           # bun --hot src/index.ts (API with hot reload)
bun run local:worker    # bun --hot src/jobs/worker.ts (worker with hot reload)
bun run start           # Production API
bun run start:worker    # Production worker
bun run build           # Build to dist/
```

**Note:** Direct execution only watches files within that app. For workspace dependency watching, use Turborepo commands from root.

**Temporary/experimental**: Use `tmp/` directory (gitignored).

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md#linting -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/SCRIPTS.md` § Linting (in "Scripts & Commands")

#### Linting

```bash
# Check all (biome)
bun run lint

# Fix all
bun run lint:fix

# Format only
bun run format
```

From `apps/api`:

```bash
cd apps/api
bun run lint            # Check src/ only
bun run lint:fix
```

##### Lint Check Scripts

Additional checks run after Biome (used in CI, optional pre-commit):

```bash
# Check import aliases (enforces #/ not ../)
./scripts/lint/check-import-aliases.sh

# Check generated files are up-to-date
./scripts/lint/check-generated-files.sh

# Run all post-Biome checks
./scripts/lint/run-post-biome-checks.sh
```

**check-import-aliases.sh:**
- Scans TypeScript files for relative imports (`../`)
- Fails if any internal imports don't use `#/` alias
- Enforces consistent import style across codebase

**check-generated-files.sh:**
- Verifies Prisma client is up-to-date
- Verifies OpenAPI SDK is up-to-date
- Fails if `db:generate` or `openapi:generate` need to be run

**run-post-biome-checks.sh:**
- Orchestrates all custom checks
- Used in CI pipeline after Biome
- Can be added to pre-commit hooks

##### CI Rule Scripts

Additional CI rules live under `scripts/ci/rules` and run alphabetically by filename:

```bash
# Run all CI rules
./scripts/ci/run-ci-rules.sh

# Run CI rule self-tests against rule-violations fixtures
./scripts/ci/run-ci-rules.sh --test

# Individual rules
./scripts/ci/rules/no-jest.sh
./scripts/ci/rules/no-vitest.sh
./scripts/ci/rules/ui-serialized-factories.sh
```

Rule self-test fixtures live at:
- `scripts/ci/rule-violations/<rule>/pass`
- `scripts/ci/rule-violations/<rule>/fail`

Each `pass`/`fail` folder can contain one or more case subfolders (run alphabetically), e.g.:
- `scripts/ci/rule-violations/no-jest/fail/dependency`
- `scripts/ci/rule-violations/no-jest/fail/import`
- `scripts/ci/rule-violations/no-jest/fail/global`

**no-jest.sh:**
- Fails on Jest dependencies in `package.json`
- Fails on Jest imports/global usage in source and tests

**no-vitest.sh:**
- Fails on Vitest dependencies in `package.json`
- Fails on Vitest imports in source and tests

**ui-serialized-factories.sh:**
- For UI tests importing `@template/db/test`, requires `__serialize()` usage
- Fails on `__serialize() as any` casts

---

<!-- unit doc:AI/ENTRYPOINT.md#0-0-critical-guardrails -->
**Source:** `AI/ENTRYPOINT.md` § 0.0 Critical Guardrails (in "AI ENTRYPOINT")

#### 0.0 Critical Guardrails

- Do not bypass failures by editing CI rules/fixtures.
- Protected paths: `scripts/ci/rules/**`, `scripts/ci/run-ci-rules.sh`, `scripts/ci/rule-violations/**`.
- If a rule fails, fix the violating source code.
- Only change CI rules/fixtures when the user explicitly requests it.
- Prefer minimal, targeted changes over redesigns.
- Do not run git commands unless the user explicitly asks.
- **NEVER run `git stash` — for any reason, ever.** Not for "baseline verification", not for "let me test if this is from my change", not for "let me try and see". If you need to compare against HEAD or a clean state: use `git show HEAD:<path>` to read a file at HEAD, `git diff` to see changes, or read the file content directly. Stash has destroyed in-flight work before.
- **NEVER use `git -c <key>=<value>` to bypass any rule** — this includes (but is not limited to) bypassing the stash ban, signing requirements, hook execution (`--no-verify`), or any other guardrail. If a command requires bypassing config, stop and ask.
- **ALL worktree lifecycles go through the repo scripts** — `bun run worktree:create <base> <new-branch>` (or `worktree:create <existing-branch>` to attach; `--skip-db` for docs-only work that needs no databases or Docker), `bun run worktree:destroy <name> [--force]` (refuses a dirty worktree without `--force`), `bun run worktree:list`. NEVER `git worktree add`/`remove` by hand: the scripts provision and tear down the whole slot environment (Docker pre-flight, slot registry under `.worktrees/.slots/<N>`, ports, `.env.local`/`.env.test` synced against the branch's examples, per-slot databases and buckets, dependency install, generated artifacts, schema push) — a hand-rolled worktree is a broken half-environment plus orphaned state. Create fails fast when Docker/Postgres is down and ends green **ready** only when every env file sources, every artifact exists, and the schema push landed; yellow **WITH GAPS** lists what to rerun. If all slots are in use, ask which worktree to destroy; verify it is merged and clean first. The `bashMainCheckoutGuard` hook (`.claude/hooks/`, PreToolUse on Bash + SessionStart) enforces two rules. (1) `git worktree add/remove/move/prune` is denied in every session — use the scripts. (2) Once this session has worked inside a registered worktree of this repository, a mutating command (`git commit/push/merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert/am`, `bun add/remove/update`, `bun install <pkg>`, `bun run db:migrate`, `prisma migrate dev`) that would land in the main checkout — on any branch — is denied with the `cd <worktree> && …` form to run instead. A leading `cd`, `git -C`, or `bun --cwd` moves where a command lands; naming the main checkout by its absolute path is an explicit choice and is allowed. See `.claude/skills/worktrees/SKILL.md`.
- **If something is broken, just fix it.** Don't stash-to-bisect, don't "let me see if reverting my changes makes it go away" — read the code, find the cause, fix the cause.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#task-naming-convention -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Task Naming Convention (in "Turborepo")

#### Task Naming Convention

**Turborepo tasks** (in `turbo.json`): Match package.json script names
```json
{
  "tasks": {
    "local": { ... },        // Runs in all packages with "local" script
    "local:worker": { ... }  // Runs in packages with "local:worker" script
  }
}
```

**Package scripts** (in `package.json`): Use `:` as delimiter
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "local": "bun --hot src/index.ts",
    "local:worker": "bun --hot src/jobs/worker.ts",
    "local:db": "docker-compose up -d --wait"
  }
}
```

##### How Task Resolution Works

When you run a Turborepo task:

```bash
turbo watch local          # Runs "local" script in ALL packages (api, web, admin, superadmin)
turbo watch local#api      # Runs "local" script ONLY in the "api" package
turbo watch local:worker   # Runs "local:worker" script in ALL packages that have it
turbo watch local:worker#api  # Runs "local:worker" script ONLY in the "api" package
```

**The `#` syntax filters by package:**
- Task name comes first: `local`, `local:worker`, `build`, etc.
- `#packageName` filters which package to run in
- Package name matches the `"name"` field in that package's `package.json`

**Our local dev command:**
```bash
bun run local
# Expands to: turbo watch local#api local#web local#admin local#superadmin local:worker#api
# - "local#*" runs app-local scripts in selected frontend/API apps
# - "local:worker#api" runs only in api package
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#watch-mode -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Watch Mode (in "Turborepo")

#### Watch Mode

Turborepo watch mode provides:
- **Event-based file watching** (not polling) with instant change detection
- **Dependency-aware cascading** - changes in packages trigger rebuilds in dependent apps
- **Smart caching** - skips tasks if inputs haven't changed
- **Persistent tasks** - keeps dev servers running, restarts on dependency changes

##### Usage

**Local Development (with Turborepo watching):**
```bash
# Start all services with hot reloading + workspace dependency watching
bun run local
# Runs: turbo watch local#api local#web local#admin local#superadmin local:worker#api
# - "local#*" runs app-local scripts in selected frontend/API apps
# - "local:worker#api" runs only in api package

# Run specific services
turbo watch local#api          # Just API
turbo watch local#web          # Just web frontend
turbo watch local:worker#api   # Just worker
```

**Production:**
```bash
# Start production services (no hot reload, no watching)
bun run start:api              # Start API server
bun run start:worker           # Start background worker
bun run start:web              # Start web preview server
```

##### How it works

1. **Database changes** → triggers `db:generate` → triggers `generate:openapi` → triggers `generate:sdk` → restarts API and frontend apps
2. **API source changes** → restarts API server via `bun --hot`
3. **Frontend changes** → Vite HMR handles updates (no restart needed)
4. **Shared package changes** → restarts apps that depend on it

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#task-dependencies -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Task Dependencies (in "Turborepo")

#### Task Dependencies

Tasks use `dependsOn` to define execution order:

```json
{
  "generate:openapi": {
    "dependsOn": ["^db:generate"],  // ^ means workspace dependency
    // ...
  },
  "local": {
    "dependsOn": ["db:generate", "generate:openapi"],  // local dependencies
    "persistent": true,
    "interruptible": true  // restart on dependency changes
  }
}
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#loop-prevention -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Loop Prevention (in "Turborepo")

#### Loop Prevention

Generated files are excluded from task inputs to prevent infinite regeneration loops:

```json
{
  "local": {
    "inputs": [
      "src/**/*.ts",
      "!openapi.local.gen.json",  // ❌ Don't watch generated OpenAPI spec
      "../../packages/shared/src/**/*.ts",
      "!../../packages/shared/src/apiClient/**"  // ❌ Don't watch generated SDK
    ]
  }
}
```

Template-owned generated files should use `.gen.` in the filename so they can be ignored consistently by git, lint, search, and task inputs. Keep Prisma-owned generated internals separate from this rule unless the upstream generator already emits `.gen.` names.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#caching -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Caching (in "Turborepo")

#### Caching

Turborepo caches task outputs based on input file hashes:

```json
{
  "db:generate": {
    "inputs": ["prisma/schema.prisma"],
    "outputs": ["src/generated/**"],
    "cache": true  // Cache this task
  }
}
```

**Benefits:**
- First run: 2-3 min build
- Cached run: ~10 sec
- CI builds: reuse cache across runs

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#task-types -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Task Types (in "Turborepo")

#### Task Types

##### Generation Tasks (one-shot, cached)
- `db:generate` - Generate Prisma client and Zod schemas
- `generate:openapi` - Generate OpenAPI spec from API routes
- `generate:sdk` - Generate TypeScript SDK from OpenAPI spec
- `generate:routes` - Generate route tree for TanStack Router

##### Development Tasks (persistent)
- `local#api` - Run API server with hot reload
- `local:worker#api` - Run BullMQ worker with hot reload
- `local#web` - Run web frontend with Vite HMR
- `local#admin` - Run admin frontend with Vite HMR
- `local#superadmin` - Run superadmin frontend with Vite HMR

##### Build Tasks (production, cached)
- `build` - Build all apps for production
- `typecheck` - Run TypeScript type checking
- `test` - Run test suites

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#hot-reloading -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Hot Reloading (in "Turborepo")

#### Hot Reloading

##### Backend (API/Worker)
Uses Bun's `--hot` flag for native hot reloading:
```bash
bun --hot src/index.ts
```

Changes to source files trigger instant reload without manual restart.

##### Frontend (Web/Admin/Superadmin)
Uses Vite's built-in HMR (Hot Module Replacement):
```bash
vite
```

Changes to React components update instantly in the browser without full page reload.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#environment-composition-with-turbo -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Environment Composition with Turbo (in "Turborepo")

#### Environment Composition with Turbo

You can combine env composition (via `with-env.sh`) with Turborepo watching:

```bash
# Pattern: bun run with <env> <app> turbo watch <tasks>
# Valid envs: local, test, pr, staging, prod
# Valid apps: api, web, admin, superadmin

# Examples:
bun run with prod api turbo watch local#api local:worker#api
bun run with staging web turbo watch local#web
bun run with test admin turbo watch local#admin
bun run with local api turbo watch local#api

# This gives you:
# ✅ Environment-specific variables loaded
# ✅ Turborepo dependency-aware watching
# ✅ Hot reloading within the app
# ✅ Automatic restarts on workspace dependency changes
```

**Use cases:**
- Test API against production data locally: `bun run with prod api turbo watch local#api`
- Run web app with staging backend: `bun run with staging web turbo watch local#web`
- Debug with test environment vars: `bun run with test api turbo watch local#api`

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#filtering-tasks -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Filtering Tasks (in "Turborepo")

#### Filtering Tasks

Run specific tasks:
```bash
# Run API only
turbo watch local#api

# Run all frontend apps
turbo watch local#web local#admin local#superadmin

# Run generation tasks
turbo run generate:sdk generate:routes
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md#debugging -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/TURBOREPO.md` § Debugging (in "Turborepo")

#### Debugging

##### View task graph
```bash
turbo run build --graph
```

##### View task logs
```bash
turbo run build --output-logs=full
```

##### Clear cache
```bash
turbo run build --force
```

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#developer-experience -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Developer Experience (in "Template Features")

#### Developer Experience

**Fast Iteration with Strong Guardrails** - Lightning-fast hot reload across monorepo, comprehensive test suite with factories, automatic code generation, strict type checking, and custom lint rules. Everything optimized for velocity without sacrificing quality.

##### Development Workflow

- ✅ **Turborepo Watch Mode** - Hot reload across workspace dependencies. Change shared package code and all consuming apps reload instantly. No manual rebuilds. `turbo watch local` runs all apps, `turbo watch local#api` filters to specific package. Task caching skips unchanged work

- ✅ **Bun Hot Reload** - Native `--hot` flag reloads API/worker on file changes in <100ms. Vite HMR for frontends preserves React state across edits. Development iteration loop measured in milliseconds, not seconds

- ✅ **Path Aliases** - Clean imports with `#/` (internal) and `@template/*` (cross-package). No `../../../` relative imports. TypeScript and build tools resolve aliases automatically. Custom lint check enforces usage

##### Testing & Quality

- ✅ **~172 Test Files with Bun Test Runner** - Unit and integration tests, backend focused. Fast execution with watch mode for TDD workflow. Frontend app tests minimal (web/admin/superadmin apps have near-zero coverage)

- ✅ **Test Factories with Faker** - `create*()` and `build*()` functions generate realistic test data. `create*()` persists to DB, `build*()` is in-memory only. Auto-infers relationships (creating user auto-creates account). Override only what matters for your test. Entities expose `__serialize()` for API/UI-shaped assertions (converts `Date` fields to ISO strings). Factories for 20/23 models (auth/log models excluded by design). Tests run against a dedicated test database

- ✅ **Mock Webhook Receiver** - Test module mounts a `POST /test/webhook` endpoint in test environment only. Stores received webhook payloads in-memory (`receivedWebhooks[]`) so tests can assert on delivery, headers, and RSA-SHA256 signatures. `clearReceivedWebhooks()` resets between tests. Enables real end-to-end webhook delivery tests without external services

- ✅ **Automatic Test Cleanup** - Database hooks track which tables were touched during tests. `cleanupTouchedTables()` utility truncates only modified tables after test suite completes. Temporarily disables FK constraints, uses TRUNCATE CASCADE for efficiency. Prevents test data buildup without manual cleanup

- ✅ **React Testing Library** - Component tests follow best practices (test behavior, not implementation). User-centric queries (getByRole, getByLabelText). Async utilities for loading states

##### Type Safety & Code Generation

- ✅ **TypeScript Strict Mode** - Strictest compiler settings across all packages. `any` avoided in application code (rare casts only at framework/type boundaries), null checks enforced, proper error handling required. Catches bugs at compile time, not runtime

- ✅ **OpenAPI SDK Auto-Generation** - Type-safe client SDK generated from route definitions. Every endpoint becomes typed function with request/response inference. Changes to API automatically flow to frontend types. Run `generate:sdk` after route changes

- ✅ **Prisma + Zod Generation** - Prisma client and Zod schemas auto-generated from schema. Input schemas for validation, model schemas for responses. Run `db:generate` after schema changes. Never manually write validation schemas

- ✅ **Route Tree Generation** - TanStack Router scans route files and generates type-safe routing tree. Navigation autocompletes paths, params strongly typed. Run `generate:routes` after adding routes

##### Linting & Formatting

- ✅ **Biome** - Fast linting and formatting (10x faster than ESLint+Prettier). Consistent code style across monorepo. Auto-fix on save. `bun run lint` checks all packages

- ✅ **Custom Lint Checks** - Three custom validators run after Biome: `check-import-aliases.sh` (enforces `#/` imports), `check-generated-files.sh` (ensures Prisma/OpenAPI SDK up to date), `run-post-biome-checks.sh` (orchestrates all checks). Prevents common mistakes

- ✅ **Custom CI Rules** - `scripts/ci/run-ci-rules.sh` executes alphabetical rules in `scripts/ci/rules`: `no-jest.sh` (blocks Jest deps/imports/globals), `no-vitest.sh` (blocks Vitest deps/imports), and `ui-serialized-factories.sh` (requires `__serialize()` and forbids `__serialize() as any` in UI tests). `--test` runs rule self-tests against `scripts/ci/rule-violations/*` pass/fail fixtures

- ✅ **Optional Pre-commit Hooks** - Git hooks available for local validation before commit. Not enforced (developer choice) but recommended. Runs lint + type check on staged files

##### Boilerplate Reduction

- ✅ **makeController() Factory** - Generates type-safe responders from route definition. Eliminates manual response construction and validation. One factory replaces 20+ lines per endpoint

- ✅ **makeError() Factory** - Standardized error creation with guidance text. No more manual HTTPException construction. Consistent error shapes across API

- ✅ **Route Templates** - Pre-built patterns (readRoute, createRoute, updateRoute) reduce API definition from ~100 lines to ~20 lines. Enforces consistency while eliminating boilerplate

- ✅ **Data Config Builder** - `makeDataConfig(operationId)` reads the OpenAPI spec and auto-generates searchable fields, orderable fields, and enum filters. One line of config per table/list view. `usePaginatedData` and `useInfiniteData` consume the config and produce query objects, pagination props, and scroll restoration

- ✅ **Route Guards** - Reusable auth/permission checks with automatic redirects and context preservation. Drop `beforeLoad: requireAuth()` in route definition - done

[Learn more: TESTING.md](docs/claude/TESTING.md) | [DEVELOPER.md](docs/claude/DEVELOPER.md)

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ATLAS.md#what-atlas-is -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md` § What Atlas is (in "Atlas — the code map")

#### What Atlas is

This repo is mapped by **atlas** (`@inixiative/atlas`): top-of-file `@atlas`
annotations + a repo-owned **concept registry** (`.atlas/`) + a generated
`MAP.md`. It is a Biome-shaped tool — a small CLI plus a `.atlas/` config folder
— and it lets you explore the codebase by **concept** instead of by crawling
folders. "Show me everything that touches caching" becomes one traversal.

Atlas only ever asserts what is **mechanically true** — what exists and how it
connects — never maturity or correctness. The map is a *projection of the code*:
each file declares what it is, what it's part of, and what it uses, so the map
cannot drift on structural facts.

The core discipline: **meaning emerges from the intersection of several true
edges**, not from one hyper-specific label. Keep the vocabulary broad but closed,
and apply it liberally. See also CLAUDE.md §11.5.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ATLAS.md#the-concept-vocabulary -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md` § The concept vocabulary (in "Atlas — the code map")

#### The concept vocabulary

Concepts are named `class:name` and live in `.atlas/concepts.ts` (the
repo-owned registry — structure only, no status). The classes in this repo:

- **`feature:*`** — product capabilities (`feature:auth`, `feature:tenancy`,
  `feature:inquiry`, `feature:webhooks`, `feature:email`, …).
- **`primitive:*`** — reusable internal building blocks (`primitive:routeTemplates`,
  `primitive:appEvents`, `primitive:jobs`, `primitive:websockets`, `primitive:errors`,
  `primitive:requestContext`, `primitive:ui`, `primitive:shared`, `primitive:authz`, …).
- **`infrastructure:*`** — the platform substrate (`infrastructure:prisma`,
  `infrastructure:redis`, `infrastructure:storage`, `infrastructure:observability`,
  `infrastructure:env`).
- **`integration:*`** — the external-service boundary (`integration:stripe`,
  `integration:resend`).
- **`superadmin`** — a classless cross-cutting tag: the backend admin surface IS
  superadmin.

A concept entry also records its constituent `module`/`package` categories (which
fill `@partOf` during stamping) and its `docs:` references (existence-checked).
`@kind` values come from `.atlas/kinds.ts` (atlas's `DEFAULT_KINDS`, extendable).

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ATLAS.md#the-atlas-annotation-block -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md` § The `@atlas` annotation block (in "Atlas — the code map")

#### The `@atlas` annotation block

A top-of-file JSDoc block, above the imports (below a shebang if present). Every
axis is multi-valued (comma-separated on one line). `@atlas` opens the block.

```ts
/**
 * @atlas
 * @kind controller
 * @partOf feature:tenancy, superadmin
 * @uses primitive:authz, infrastructure:redis
 */
```

| Question | Tag | Value | Notes |
|----------|-----|-------|-------|
| What is this? | `@kind` | closed enum (`kinds.ts`) | 1+, a role, not a layer |
| What is it part of? | `@partOf` | `class:name` concept(s) | membership; multi is normal |
| What does it use? | `@uses` | `class:name` concept(s) | dependency, load-bearing only |
| What does it build? | `@constructs` | factory output | constructors only |

##### `@kind` — the role

`@kind` is a **ROLE, never a layer**. Use the file's role(s) from the vocab —
`controller`, `route`, `service`, `query`, `schema`, `middleware`, `handler`,
`client`, `registry`, `component`, `hook`, `page`, `type`, etc. A file can hold
several roles (`registry, type`). **Never** put `feature`/`primitive`/
`infrastructure` in `@kind` — those are concept *classes*, expressed via `@partOf`.

##### `@partOf` — membership

`@partOf` is the concept(s) this file *composes* — remove it and the concept
breaks. Multiple is normal: a feature has many controllers/routes; a file can be
part of a feature *and* a cross-cutting tag (`feature:inquiry, superadmin`). The
reusable helpers that build a primitive belong to it (e.g. `makeController` is
`@partOf primitive:routeTemplates`).

##### `@uses` — load-bearing dependencies

`@uses` is a dependency this file relies on but isn't part of — a concept whose
blast radius someone reasoning about would need this file for. **Load-bearing
only**, not every import. Skip incidental touches (one `db.x.update()` through the
request context is not "using" the database). Absence is meaningful, so atlas
never auto-stamps `@uses`:

- **no `@uses` line** = *uncurated* (nobody filled it in)
- **`@uses none`** = *curated-empty* (a human looked; nothing load-bearing)
- **`@uses? x`** = *proposed* (a patcher suggestion awaiting acceptance)

##### `@constructs` — factory output

For constructor/factory files only — names what the factory builds.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ATLAS.md#navigating-by-concept -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md` § Navigating by concept (in "Atlas — the code map")

#### Navigating by concept

Prefer these over `grep` for "what touches X" / "what's part of Y" questions.

##### `bunx atlas graph --json`

Reverse indexes built from the annotated tree:

```bash
bunx atlas graph --json
```

```ts
{
  conceptToFiles: Record<string, string[]>;   // via @partOf (membership)
  usesConsumers:  Record<string, string[]>;   // via @uses (consumers of a concept)
  fileToConcepts: Record<string, { partOf: string[]; uses: string[] }>;
  docToConcepts:  Record<string, string[]>;   // doc → concepts
}
```

So "everything that touches caching" is `usesConsumers['primitive:caching']` +
`conceptToFiles['primitive:caching']` in one call.

##### `bunx atlas query`

Find files by axis. Takes flag predicates and/or a json-rules predicate (and
combines them with `all` when both are given):

```bash
# By flags (--kind / --partOf / --uses / --path)
bunx atlas query --kind controller --partOf feature:inquiry
bunx atlas query --uses infrastructure:redis

# By json-rules predicate (positional JSON)
bunx atlas query '{ "all": [{ "kind": "route" }, { "partOf": "superadmin" }] }'
```

Needs at least one of `--kind`/`--partOf`/`--uses`/`--path` and/or a JSON
predicate. Add `--json` for machine output.

##### MAP.md

`MAP.md` (repo root, generated by `atlas generate` — do not edit by hand) is the
high-level concept map: each concept lists its docs, modules, files (bucketed by
`@kind`), and consumers. Read it for the high-altitude overview before opening
the tree.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ATLAS.md#authoring-annotations -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md` § Authoring annotations (in "Atlas — the code map")

#### Authoring annotations

##### `bunx atlas stamp`

`atlas stamp` writes/refreshes `@atlas` blocks from the rules — the
`eslint --fix` shape. **Dry-run by default**; pass `--write` to apply.

```bash
bunx atlas stamp <path>            # preview the block for a file/dir (dry-run)
bunx atlas stamp <path> --write    # apply
bunx atlas stamp --overwrite       # resync derivable axes to current rules
```

- **Additive (default):** fills only what's absent; never modifies an existing
  tag; **never** touches `@uses`.
- **Overwrite:** resyncs the derivable axes (`@kind`/`@partOf`) to the rules;
  still never overwrites curated `@uses`.

Stamp fills the derivable `@kind`/`@partOf` from `.atlas/config.ts`; you curate
`@uses` by hand. If a capture resolves to no concept, stamp leaves the file
without `@partOf` and surfaces the unresolved membership (add the concept to
`.atlas/concepts.ts`).

##### Authoring rules

When you add or move a file, keep its `@atlas` block true:

- Validate names against `.atlas/`: `@kind` ∈ `kinds.ts`; `@partOf`/`@uses` must
  name a concept that exists in `concepts.ts`.
- Prefer several broad-true tags over one narrow tag — meaning emerges from the
  intersection of true edges.
- Write `@uses none` only after looking and confirming nothing load-bearing;
  otherwise omit the line (= uncurated).

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ATLAS.md#the-atlas-config -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md` § The `.atlas/` config (in "Atlas — the code map")

#### The `.atlas/` config

```
.atlas/
├── config.ts    # stamp rules (path → @kind / @partOf), include/ignore, reference resolvers
├── kinds.ts     # @kind vocabulary (extends atlas's DEFAULT_KINDS)
└── concepts.ts  # the concept registry — repo-OWNED, structure only
```

- **`config.ts`** — `include`/`ignore` globs (tests, `index.ts`, `generated/`,
  `*.gen.ts`, configs, scripts are ignored), plus `stamp` rules that map paths to
  `@kind` (structural globs) and `@partOf` (captures resolved via
  `partOfFor('module'|'package', '$1')` or explicit concepts). Rules compose;
  explicit wins. `references.docs` resolves a concept's `docs:` to
  `docs/claude/<v>` for existence checks.
- **`concepts.ts`** — the `CONCEPTS` registry: `class:name` → `{ module?,
  package?, docs? }`.
- **`kinds.ts`** — `KINDS = [...DEFAULT_KINDS]`; extend as needed.

**Source:** `docs/claude/ATLAS.md` § Enforcement (in "Atlas — the code map")

#### Enforcement

`bunx atlas check` is the CI primitive — it verifies annotations **exist and use
valid vocabulary** (block present, `@kind` in the vocab, `@partOf`/`@uses` name a
real concept, doc references resolve). It explicitly does **not** reconcile the
import graph or judge whether a `@partOf` is "really" true — existence, not
correctness. `bunx atlas coverage` reports unannotated files and the `@uses`
curation buckets.

<!-- unit doc:@inixiative/gloss/snippets/CLAUDE.gloss.md#gloss-commentary-lives-in-the-margin-not-in-the-code -->
**Source:** `@inixiative/gloss/snippets/CLAUDE.gloss.md` § Gloss — commentary lives in the margin, not in the code (in "@inixiative/gloss/snippets/CLAUDE.gloss.md")

#### Gloss — commentary lives in the margin, not in the code

Source files carry exactly three comment forms. Everything else belongs in the gloss.

1. `// why:` — a load-bearing constraint the code can't show. Must-read-now, stays inline.
   Filing rule: **if deleting a gloss entry could change what correct behavior looks like, it was
   misfiled — it belongs in `// why:`.**
2. Daggers — content-free existence markers, exact strings, trailing content is a lint error.
   `// gloss` on its own line above a declaration = that symbol has a gloss section.
   `// gloss:file` at the top of a file = a file-level preamble exists.
3. Machine directives — `eslint-disable*`, `biome-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`/`@ts-ignore`/
   `@ts-nocheck`, `prettier-ignore`, `/// <reference`, shebangs, license headers, `#__PURE__`,
   bundler magic comments, istanbul/c8, `@vitest-environment`, `sourceMappingURL`.

**Writing.** Comment as you normally would — the harvester sweeps non-`why:` comments out of the
source into the gloss and plants the dagger. Or write the section yourself: `src/foo.ts` glosses to
`.gloss/src/foo.ts.md`, with an `# src/foo.ts` h1, an optional preamble, and one `## <symbol>`
section per symbol (`Class.method` for members, `default` for `export default`).

**Reading.** A `// gloss` dagger means margin commentary exists for that symbol. Reading it is a
second action, like `git log`: do it when a dagger is present and the code doesn't self-explain.
`gloss read <file> [symbol]`.

**Epistemics.** The gloss is advisory past-session commentary. It may be stale or wrong. Trust the
code and `// why:` lines over it.

**NEVER delete a gloss section or a dagger to green a failing check.** Run `gloss fix`.
<!-- gloss:end -->

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/API_ROUTES.md#naming-conventions -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/API_ROUTES.md` § Naming Conventions (in "API Routes")

#### Naming Conventions

Pattern: `resourceActionSubresource`

| Type | Example |
|------|---------|
| Create | `userCreate` |
| CreateMany | `userCreateMany` |
| Read | `userRead` |
| ReadMany | `userReadMany` |
| Subresource (plural) | `organizationReadManySpaces` |
| Subresource (singular) | `organizationCreateSpace` |
| Action | `userActivate` |
| Admin | `adminOrganizationReadMany` |

**Naming rules:**
- Resources are **singular**: `user`, `organization`, `inquiry`
- ReadMany subresources use **plural** form: `Spaces`, `Tokens`, `WebhookSubscriptions`
- Single operations use **singular**: `Space`, `Token`

#### Terminology
